title: Feedback Capacity and a Variant of the Kalman Filter with ARMA Gaussian Noises: Explicit Bounds and Feedback Coding Design
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a control and information-theoretic problem: how to characterize the feedback capacity of additive colored Gaussian noise channels when the noise follows a finite-order ARMA process. The authors aim to derive explicit lower bounds on feedback capacity and to provide feedback coding schemes that can achieve those bounds.

The central approach is to connect the feedback-channel problem to a variant of the Kalman filter. By reformulating an ARMA-noise channel as an equivalent Kalman filtering system, the paper derives structural conditions under which the closed-loop system yields a lower bound on feedback capacity. The analysis is developed for general finite-order ARMA measurement noise, with special attention to first-order ARMA and second-order MA cases.

The paper does not study a human or educational population; it is a mathematical/theoretical contribution in communication theory. Its main conclusions are that the proposed bounds are consistent with and, in some special cases, tight relative to prior results in the literature. The authors also derive recursive coding schemes based on the Kalman-filter interpretation, and they note that the framework may be extended in future work to obtain tighter bounds or broader structural insights.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a theoretical/control-theory paper on feedback capacity in Gaussian communication channels, not an empirical study of educational technology or teacher coaching. It contains no study design, participants, or educational intervention evaluation relevant to the retrieval topic.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no measured educational impact, effect size, or practical intervention outcome related to teacher planning, feedback quality, or instructional coaching. The paper does not provide evidence of positive or negative impact on the requested education outcomes.
